A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PSM research despite the changed title and format. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original gridworld, FetchReach, and continuous-control experiments in Section 7, plus dimensionality ablations and policy-error measurements in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revised Cheetah results in Table 1.

M1.justification: The affine successor-measure representation, discrete policy codebook, joint training, and constrained inference procedure remain unchanged. Equation 7 gains a squared residual, but that squared loss already appears in v1's unchanged Appendix B.3.2 pseudocode; this does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same gridworld, four-room, FetchReach, and ExoRL Walker, Cheetah, Quadruped, and Pointmass tasks. Appendix C retains the same environment and task coverage.

E2.justification: Laplacian and FB remain the gridworld and FetchReach comparators. Continuous-control Table 1 includes Laplacian, FB, and HILP in both versions; explicitly adding HILP to the introductory baseline list does not introduce a new evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The reported data collection, representation dimensions, training budgets, discounts, episode lengths, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 7 and Appendices B–C. The new significance test does not establish a change to the experimental design.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 retains the same Walker/Cheetah dimensionality ablation at d = 32, 50, 128, and 256. Appendix C.2 retains the same policy-error analysis, and the qualitative gridworld and FetchReach analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 adds significance markers to the environment-average rows and specifies a Mann–Whitney U test at level 0.05. The existing five-seed and three-seed reporting remains unchanged. The new caption does not identify comparison pairs or provide p-values.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes all four PSM Cheetah results under the same reported settings: for example, Walk changes from 887.02 ± 59.87 to 984.21 ± 0.49, and the environment average from 607.61 to 626.01. Appendix Table 3 retains the earlier d = 128 values, creating an inconsistency. Section 7.1 also removes the explicit 100% success statement; the remaining benchmark and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.4 explicitly introduces the span over possible rewards and qualifies the inclusion with 'for some Φ'. Appendix A.3 revises the inclusion argument and adds a construction and separate separability discussion. Equations 1–3 adopt marginal flow constraints already developed in Appendix A, while Equation 7 restores the squared residual. These are targeted revisions to existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The main claims remain representation of all possible behaviors through policy-independent bases, efficient joint learning, and zero-shot optimal-policy inference for arbitrary rewards. The abstract's shift from 'solutions' and 'policies' to visitation-based 'behaviors' clarifies terminology without changing the research scope or listed contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 replaces 'marked improvement' over baselines across most environments with the more qualified interpretation that PSM performs better or competitively. The explanations involving FB overestimation and the limitations concerning representation size and dataset coverage remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the architectures, hyperparameters, pseudocode, hardware, training times, and data/code references. Although Section 7.1 trims the explicit state-only successor-measure explanation, its formulation remains documented in the equations and pseudocode. The displayed project address is corrected, but the embedded link destination is identical.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained, but Sections 1–2 qualify the criticism that random-policy Laplacian features cannot represent all value functions to 'usually' cannot. Section 2 also describes PSM's policy as optimal rather than near-optimal. These are limited positioning changes.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'Representing the Behavior Space of an RL Agent', with localized abstract edits, terminology changes, and revised experimental signposting. A generic Impact Statement replaces the acknowledgements. The overall section sequence and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout with new typography and running headers. Figures are resized and repositioned; Table 1 gains rotated environment labels and sits beside Figure 4, whose image and plot are rearranged vertically. All six figures and four tables are retained rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves consistency between Equation 7 and the existing pseudocode, clarifies the flow formulation, and adds significance-test reporting. However, its revised Table 1 contradicts the retained Cheetah results in Appendix Table 3. The expanded A.3 proof also uses a summed-reward normalizer with a diagonal basis that selects only r(s), leaving the new construction algebraically unresolved. These improvements and reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net quality change.
